newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on seeding prospects.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on seeding prospects.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended lower on spillover pressure from other markets and on improved planting prospects in the northern U.S. Plains, traders said.

"Generally, planting prospects pressured the board in corn, wheat and beans. We've run prices up pretty well over the last month, but it'll be unsustainable if we get the crop in the ground," an MGE trader said.
Meteorology firm Weather Services Corp said Monday it expected no heavy precipitation in the northern U.S. Plains over the next few days.
Spring wheat also drew pressure from other markets, particularly KCBT wheat, in which the May contract dropped sharply on fund long liquidation.
Wheat also weakened on improved crop weather in Europe and in the U.S. hard red winter wheat belt, traders said.
MGE spring wheat settled eight to 11-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with May down eight cents at $4.32-1/2. New crop September lost 10 cents to close at $4.32-3/4.
